fields.description: Program Description Brief Introduction With remarkable expansion of the number of foreign students coming to the university, GDUT provides a wide range of Chinese language programs on various levels of learning and training. Students are expected to improve Chinese proficiency at the end of each program with a closer look into the tradition and custom, to communicate with native Chinese, and to obtain sufficient skills and knowledge in the areas of HSK Tests. In addition, special-designed course work tailored to the needs of certain students may also be provided and arranged. Teaching Objective To acquaint students with the essentials of Chinese language, including consonants, vowels, intonation, pronunciation, Chinese character writing, commonly used vocabulary and basic grammar. To develop student's ability in listening, speaking, writing and translating, and prepare students both linguistically and culturally for daily contact with Chinese people. To promote the ability to successfully pass the HSK Test. Courses and Candidates Class Candidates Compulsory Courses Elective Courses Elementary Chinese(1) for beginners Basic Chinese intensive reading; Chinese listening comprehension for beginners; basic Chinese reading; Chinese Characters; Basic oral Chinese, etc. Chinese Painting, Chinese Calligraphy, Chinese folk songs and music, Martial Arts, Chinese History and Geography, Survey of China, Computerized Information Processing, Cantonese, etc. Elementary Chinese(2) for students who have studied Chinese language for 4-6 months, or as an equivalent to HSK Grade 2; Intermediate Chinese(1) for students who have studied Chinese language for 10-12 months, or as an equivalent to HSK Grade 3; Intermediate Chinese intensive reading, Intermediate Chinese extensive reading, Intermediate spoken Chinese, basic Chinese writing. Chinese grammar, etc. Intermediate Chinese(2) for students who have studied Chinese language for 16-18 months, or as an equivalent to HSK Grade 4; Advanced Chinese(1) for students who have studied Chinese language for 2 years, or as an equivalent to the level of HSK Grade 5; Advanced Chinese (1) is equivalent to the level of the third academic year of a four year study. Advanced Chinese, Audio-Visual Chinese, Advanced Chinese extensive reading, Survey of China, An Introduction to Chinese culture, Business Chinese, etc. Advanced Chinese(2) for students who have studied Chinese language for 2 years, or as an equivalent to the level of HSK Grade 6; Advanced Chinese (1) is equivalent to the level of the fourth academic year of a four year study. Class Time Morning:8:30-12:00, Afternoon:13:30-16:30(Monday-Friday). Notes : 1) The long-term class students should attend a class-dividing test. We have examinations twice a semester, and the test result will decide which class you are in. 2) If students complete their lessons within the period of study, certificate will be granted. 3) Students have the right to choose the classes and courses according to their own interest and language levels. 4)Notes For students who applied within one month or after the starting date: -If you are a beginner, you may need to wait until the university gets enough students to open a beginner class(there will be uncertainties). -If you have learned Chinese before, you might be able to come to China and study with the current class directly. -If you want one-semester program only but are only able to come to China when there is a very short time left, you are advised to switch to 1 1-year program. If you insist on only want one-semester program and are ok with just learn for the remaining time, it is also ok.

fields.materials: Application Materials " * " means necessary documents that you must provide in your application. If you want to book our translation service , please pay and book it at least 2 weeks before the application deadline for submission of all documents; If you want to book our guardian service , you need to pay and book it 2 months before the application deadline, just in case your application fails because of failed to submit application documents in time. * 1. Ordinary Passport -A clear, full-color scan of your passport information page, showing your name, passport number, expiration date, and photo. -Some universities may also require blank visa pages, so you are advised to upload a few blank pages as well. -Your passport must have a validity of more than one year. * 2. Highest Degree Graduation Certificate -A formal graduation certificate of your highest completed education level (e.g., Senior High School, Bachelor’s, or Master’s degree). -If the document is not in Chinese or English, it must be translated into Chinese or English and notarized by an authorized translation agency or relevant authority. Self-translations are not accepted. * 3. Highest Degree Academic Transcripts -Formal academic transcripts of your highest completed education level (e.g., Senior High School, Bachelor’s, or Master’s degree), covering ALL academic years, NOT just the final year. -If the document is not in Chinese or English, it must be translated into Chinese or English and notarized by an authorized translation agency or relevant authority. Self-translations are not accepted. * 4. Non-criminal Record Certificate -Please note that this document is valid for only 3 months. For instance, if you submit your -application in April, your non-criminal record must have been issued no earlier than January. -Obtain a police clearance certificate from the local police station where you currently reside, confirming no criminal record in the past 6 months at the time of application. -You need to translated it into CHINESE if it is not in Chinese; Then you need to get it notarized by local notary office and then get it certified by local Chinese embassy; If your country has joined the HAGUE convention then just do the Chinese translation and Apostille; Then you may need to mail original copy of non-criminal record and translation & certified(or Apostille) documents to the university in China. -If you are currently in China, the certificate must be issued by the local Chinese police. * 5. Physical Examination Form -Download the form template, print it, and bring it to a hospital for the required medical tests. The hospital will complete the form with your results. -The medical examination must cover all items listed on the form. -Ensure your photo is attached and the form is stamped and signed by the hospital after the examination. -The medical results are valid for 6 months only. -Forms that are incomplete, lack a final physician’s suggestion, missing the attending physician’s signature, official hospital stamp, or applicant’s sealed photo will be considered invalid. -The document must be in English or Chinese. You can download a template or sample from here . * 6. CV -Submit a resume or CV to help the university better understand your background. -Written in Chinese or in English. Your resume must include a complete and continuous list of your education and work experience, covering all periods up to the time you apply to university, without missing a single year or month. -Some universities may require you to use their designated CV templates, which must be downloaded and completed accordingly. You can download a template or sample from here . 7. Passport photo A recent passport-sized photo of the applicant Tips: For applicants who are in China: If you are an employee, you still need to provide employment separation certificate and your current residence permit. If you are a student, you need to provide transfer certificate, leaving certificate, certificate of attendance rate issued by previous school and your current residence permit.
fields.requirements: Entry Requirements Applicants shall reach the age of 18 years old, Applicants must be non-Chinese citizens and valid foreign passport holders, without any criminal records. Applicants shall abide by the laws and decrees of the Chinese government and related rules of university, honor the Chinese social morality and customs, and will not participate in any activities which are inappropriate to the capacity as a student.
